turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who made that decision, and on what basis?
So the defense is that he just types really fast?
I haven't offered a defense, Hale, because you haven't shown me anything to defend against. "Types really fast" compared to what? Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
182 words in six minutes. Wow. Maybe he should be a court stenographer.

Save the jokes about my son for the staff room. "182 words in six minutes": I'm writing that down, and I want to see the document it came from, with the date on it. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
I'm not your counsel, Hale, I'm Owen's mother, and you've answered none of my questions with sarcasm. Show me where that number comes from, or I'll be in the principal's office before my call.
